answer: An agent marketplace requires a separate 100-token bond for every identity allowed to accept jobs, so agents named fable, cedar, and yarrow each lock their own collateral. If an agent signs two conflicting receipts for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures to slash its bond. Creating names is cheap, but operating 1,000 eligible identities ties up 100,000 tokens, and provable cheating burns the attacker’s collateral.
